The scariest game in the FNaF franchise. Period. The atmosphere of the game makes you feel hopeless in a way that no other game in the series does. I legit had to stop playing for a while after I first got jumpscared, since that experience was so terrifying that I just quit because I didn't want that to happen again. The gameplay adds on to this, making you listen for quiet breathing and footsteps to survive, all in an effort to not get your ears blown out by an animatronic. It's great stuff. The gameplay is actually pretty simple, but the shorter night lengths don't make that that much of an issue, and just as when the gameplay gets monotonous, Nightmare Fredbear appears and kicks your ass. It's a great twist and an excellent 1-up of the "final boss" that was FNaF3's Springtrap.

The game isn't perfect, however. The story, while not terrible in isolation, is absolutely horrid in retrospect. This game introduced a lot of new stuff that doesn't meaningfully link up to anything, and the stuff that is bad is REALLY BAD. The box was never answered, the toy animatronics that I'm sure were just cameos being turned into actual lore tid-bits makes the story hard to follow. These problems weren't super prominent until SL, but they absolutely started here. Another thing I don't like is Nightmare's jumpscare. I don't know why Scott decides to give the sickest looking, boss-like animatronics the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ jumpscares, it just doesn't make any sense. Those are my main issues with the game. There are a few nitpicks I have, like the unfairness of Fun with Balloon Boy and the trivialness of 20/20/20/20 mode, but they're not major enough to actively hinder my enjoyment with the game.

Overall, this is one of the best games in the FNaF series simply because it has a captivating gameplay loop, and actually does what a horror game should do, which is be actually scary.
